vectors.name: quoted-value-carrying-an-lf-is-one-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: LF is valid inside a quoted value and is not WSP between attributes, so this is one marker whose body spans two source lines. Recognition uses the LF-normalized copy while `raw` stays the verbatim source. §3.3 judges the marker by the line it OPENS on, which is why `line` is 2 rather than 3.
vectors.text:
Para.
<!-- stay:q1 x-note="line one
line two" hash=sha256:abcd -->

markers.raw:
<!-- stay:q1 x-note="line one
line two" hash=sha256:abcd -->

vectors.name: attribute-without-a-value-is-not-a-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: `attribute = key "=" value`, so a bare token after the id is not a complete grammar match and the comment is not a valid marker for attachment, hashing, row-token recognition, or preservation evidence. The id is not the offending token, so this is NOT the malformed-marker diagnostic: nothing is reported and nothing is attached. The following marker proves the scan resumes.
vectors.text:
Para.
<!-- stay:m1 hash=sha256:abcd novalue -->
<!-- stay:ok1 hash=sha256:beef -->

vectors.name: invalid-escape-in-a-quoted-value-is-not-a-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: inside a quoted value `\"` and `\\` are the ONLY escapes, so `\n` is not a qchar and the body is not a complete match. An implementation that accepts C-style escapes reads a marker here and fails this vector.

vectors.name: an-html-body-stops-at-the-first-close
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: the host comment owns its close delimiter and double quotes do not escape `-->` from the HTML parser. The reader stops at the FIRST `-->`, leaving an unterminated quoted value, so no marker is recognized. A DOTALL regex reaching for the last `-->` on the line reads a marker here and fails.
vectors.text:
Para.
<!-- stay:m3 x-note="a --> b" -->
<!-- stay:ok3 hash=sha256:beef -->

vectors.name: an-html-body-stops-at-the-first-bang-close
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: an HTML reader stops at the earlier of `-->` and `--!>`, and only `-->` completes the production. Stopping at `--!>` leaves an incomplete body, so nothing is recognized. A reader that knows only `-->` skips past the `--!>` and reads a marker here, which is the divergence this vector exists to catch.
vectors.text:
Para.
<!-- stay:m4 x-note="a --!> b" -->
<!-- stay:ok4 hash=sha256:beef -->

vectors.name: an-mdx-body-stops-at-the-first-star-slash
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: an MDX reader stops at the first `*/` and completes only when `}` follows immediately. Here the first `*/` is inside the quoted value and is followed by a space, so the opener is rejected.

vectors.name: a-rejected-mdx-opener-does-not-consume-a-later-one
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: a rejected opener does not consume a later opener. The scan resumes from the independent opener scan rather than swallowing the valid marker on the next line. An implementation that restarts after the rejected marker's would-be end loses `good` entirely.

vectors.name: an-html-candidate-rejected-in-its-quoted-value-keeps-a-valid-inner-and-the-trailing-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: every opener is an independent candidate. `bad` opens a quoted value that is still open at the first `-->`, so it is rejected; `recovered` begins inside that value and is a complete marker of its own, and `last` follows. A scanner that memoizes the attribute grammar by position alone carries `bad`'s rejection, taken in the quoted-value state, onto `recovered`'s id characters and loses it. The memo must key the grammar state as well as the position.

vectors.name: an-mdx-candidate-rejected-in-its-quoted-value-keeps-a-valid-inner-and-the-trailing-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4, the MDX host: `bad`'s quoted value is open at the first `*/`, so it is rejected, while `recovered`, which begins inside it, is complete, and `last` follows. The memo-key fault the HTML vector above catches, in the other host's scanner.

vectors.name: a-valid-html-candidate-keeps-the-diagnostic-of-a-malformed-inner-and-the-trailing-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: `outer` is valid, its bare value running through `<!--stay:hash=abc`, and the inner candidate, which starts inside that value, has a key where its id belongs: not a marker, but the one invalid shape §4 still requires a diagnostic for, so it is reported malformed. The two share the first `-->`. A memo keyed on position alone hands `outer`'s accepting verdict to the inner candidate. The full parse that follows still refuses it as a marker, but a scanner that decides the diagnostic from the validator's verdict, before that parse, has already ruled it out, and the diagnostic is lost. This is the false-accept direction of the memo fault, and the only place it shows.

vectors.name: a-valid-mdx-candidate-keeps-the-diagnostic-of-a-malformed-inner-and-the-trailing-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4, the MDX host: the vector above, `outer` valid over a key-first inner candidate that must still be reported malformed.

vectors.name: a-malformed-html-candidate-does-not-consume-a-valid-inner-or-the-trailing-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: the outer candidate puts a key where its id belongs, so it is not a marker but is reported malformed, the one invalid shape §4 still requires a diagnostic for. It is still only a candidate: `inner`, which opens inside it and shares its `-->`, is a complete marker and is reported too, and `last` follows. A scanner that resumes after the close of anything it emitted, the diagnostic included, loses `inner`. `a-rejected-mdx-opener-does-not-consume-a-later-one` pins the rejected case, which emits nothing; this pins the case that emits a record.

vectors.name: a-malformed-mdx-candidate-does-not-consume-a-valid-inner-or-the-trailing-marker
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4, the MDX host: the vector above, a malformed outer diagnostic that must not consume the complete `inner` sharing its `*/}`.

vectors.name: an-html-candidate-over-an-mdx-marker-is-validated-against-its-own-close
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: each host reads to its own close. `h` reads `{/*stay:m` and `b=1*/}` as bare values, then meets `"x` after a space and is rejected at `-->`; `m` is a complete MDX marker ending at its own `*/}`. The two candidates reach the same positions in the same grammar states, with different closes. A scanner that shares one grammar memo between the hosts without the close in its key replays `h`'s rejection onto `m` and loses it.

vectors.name: an-mdx-candidate-over-an-html-marker-is-validated-against-its-own-close
vectors.note: SPEC.md §4: the vector above with the hosts swapped. `m` is read first and rejected at `*/}`; `h` is a complete HTML marker ending at its own `-->`, over positions `m` already visited in the same states.
